dicas.texto: Boa observação! Quando o problema diz '3/4 das pessoas', que parte da fração representa 'quantas partes do todo' estamos falando?
Você está no caminho certo! Volte ao enunciado e procure a frase exata que contém a fração. Qual número está em cima? E embaixo?
Quase lá! A fração já está escrita no texto: '3/4'. O numerador é o número antes da barra, e o denominador é o depois.
Você está quase! Veja: o enunciado diz '3/4 das pessoas'. Então, na caixa de cima (f1), digite o número antes da barra. Na de baixo (f2), digite o número depois da barra.
Pense: se o denominador é 4, em quantas partes iguais o segmento de 0 a 1 foi dividido? E quantas dessas partes você precisa contar?
Divida mentalmente o espaço entre 0 e 1 em 4 partes iguais. Comece do 0 e conte 1, 2, 3 partes — pare aí!
A reta tem encaixe exato para quartos, mesmo que as marcas não apareçam. 3/4 está mais perto do 1 do que do 0. Tente posicionar um pouco antes do final.
Você está quase! Imagine: 1/4 é um passo, 2/4 é o meio, 3/4 é um passo antes do 1. Arraste o ponto até esse lugar!

Select three of the four equal parts, then submit the fraction represented by the selected parts.

misconceptions.feedback: You used the fraction for viewers younger than 18. The requested group is viewers older than 18, so reread the sentence describing that group.

misconceptions.description: Aluno interpreta 'maiores de 18' como o complemento de 'menores de 18' e responde com a diferença (1), mas esquece o denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You focused on the amount needed to complete the whole instead of identifying the complete fraction stated for viewers older than 18.

nodes.description: Manipulate the fraction model to identify the numerator of the requested fraction.
nodes.instruction: Manipulate the fraction model to identify the numerator of the requested fraction.

hints.message: The numerator tells how many equal parts are being counted.
Look at the parts selected in the fraction model and count those parts.
Do not count all the parts in the whole; count only the parts representing the older viewers.
Count the selected parts from left to right and enter that count in the upper fraction field.

misconceptions.description: Aluno responde com o numerador da fração inicial (1/4) em vez da fração solicitada (3/4)
misconceptions.feedback: You used the numerator from the first fraction mentioned. The requested fraction describes viewers older than 18, so use the selected parts for that group.

misconceptions.description: Aluno usa o denominador (4) como numerador, por associar '4' ao número de partes totais
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the total number of equal parts. The numerator counts selected parts, while the denominator counts all parts.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator in the upper fraction box.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator in the upper fraction box.

hints.message: The top number tells how many equal parts belong to the group being described.
Use the count of selected parts from the fraction model and type it in the upper box.
The upper box should contain the count of the colored or selected parts, not the total number of parts.
Type the count of the selected parts into f1, the box above the fraction bar.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde o significado do numerador e usa o valor do denominador no campo do numerador
misconceptions.feedback: The number 4 tells how many equal parts make the whole. The upper box needs the number of selected parts.

misconceptions.description: Aluno responde com o numerador da fração inicial (1/4) em vez da fração solicitada (3/4)
misconceptions.feedback: You entered the numerator from 1/4. The requested fraction is about viewers older than 18, so use the numerator for that group.

nodes.description: Manipulate the fraction model to identify the denominator.
nodes.instruction: Manipulate the fraction model to identify the denominator.

hints.message: The denominator describes how many equal parts make the entire whole.
Count every equal section in the fraction model, including selected and unselected sections.
The denominator is based on the total partition of the model, not only on the selected portion.
Count all equal sections in the bar and enter that total in the lower fraction field.

misconceptions.description: Aluno troca numerador e denominador ao preencher os campos
misconceptions.feedback: You counted the selected parts instead of all parts in the whole. The denominator counts every equal section.

misconceptions.description: Aluno assume que o denominador deve ser 4 por causa da escala da reta, mesmo que já saiba a fração
misconceptions.feedback: The denominator must come from the total equal parts shown in the fraction model, not from assuming a value without checking the model.

nodes.description: Enter the denominator in the lower fraction box.
nodes.instruction: Enter the denominator in the lower fraction box.

hints.message: The bottom number tells how many equal parts are in the whole.
Count all equal parts in the model and place that count in the lower box.
The lower box does not show how many parts are selected; it shows how many parts exist altogether.
Type the total number of equal sections into f2, the box below the fraction bar.

misconceptions.description: Aluno troca numerador e denominador ao preencher os campos
misconceptions.feedback: You placed the numerator in the lower box. The lower box must contain the total number of equal parts.

misconceptions.description: Aluno assume que o denominador deve ser 4 por causa da escala da reta, mesmo que já saiba a fração
misconceptions.feedback: Do not choose the denominator by guessing from the number line. Use the number of equal parts in the fraction described by the problem.

nodes.description: Use the fraction model to confirm that the fraction is less than one.
nodes.instruction: Use the fraction model to confirm that the fraction is less than one.

hints.message: A fraction is less than one when the selected parts do not make the entire whole.
Compare the number of selected parts with the total number of equal parts.
Check whether the numerator is smaller than the denominator.
Confirm that the selected portion stops before the entire bar is filled, then submit the fraction shown by the model.

misconceptions.description: Aluno clica em Done sem digitar nada, ou só em um campo
misconceptions.feedback: The fraction fields were not completed correctly. Check that both the numerator and denominator are entered before submitting.

nodes.description: Mark the fraction on the number line from 0 to 1.
nodes.instruction: Mark the fraction on the number line from 0 to 1.

hints.message: The denominator tells you how many equal intervals to make between 0 and 1.
Divide the distance from 0 to 1 into four equal intervals and count three intervals from 0.
The point should be between one-half and one, closer to one.
Starting at zero, move through the first, second, and third equal intervals, then place the point at that third division.

misconceptions.description: Aluno posiciona na reta a fração que digitou incorretamente (1/4), consistente com seu erro anterior
misconceptions.feedback: You marked the first quarter, which corresponds to 1/4. The requested fraction is the third quarter of the interval.

misconceptions.description: Aluno aproxima 3/4 para 1/2 por falta de precisão ou confusão com a metade
misconceptions.feedback: You marked the midpoint. Three quarters is farther right than one-half and closer to one.

misconceptions.description: Aluno conta 3 traços/marcas e assume que é 3/4, mas o raciocínio é baseado em contagem de marcas, não em divisão do intervalo
misconceptions.feedback: Count equal intervals, not the labels as whole numbers. Three of four equal intervals corresponds to a point between zero and one.

misconceptions.description: Aluno tenta posicionar fração imprópria em reta limitada a [0,1] e coloca no limite
misconceptions.feedback: The requested fraction is less than one, so the point must be before the endpoint at one.

nodes.description: Convert the proper fraction using the Convert button.
nodes.instruction: Convert the proper fraction using the Convert button.

hints.message: A mixed number separates a whole-number part from a remaining fractional part.
Compare the numerator with the denominator to determine whether a complete whole can be removed.
Because the fraction is proper, the whole-number part does not contain a complete whole.
Enter zero as the whole-number part and keep the original numerator and denominator as the fractional part, then complete the conversion.

misconceptions.description: Aluno troca numerador e denominador ao preencher os campos
misconceptions.feedback: The numerator and denominator were reversed. Keep the selected-part count on top and the total-part count on the bottom.

misconceptions.description: Aluno clica em Done sem digitar nada, ou só em um campo
misconceptions.feedback: The converted fraction is incomplete. Check all mixed-number fields before finishing the conversion.
